note: Maps each payment-security-relevant change to the test that would fail if the behaviour regressed. 'covers' lists test files; 'case' names the specific regression case. Gaps are stated explicitly rather than implied away.

entries.case: wrong-key signature → invalid_signature (no settlement); short/malformed signature refused; 128-hex enforcement; delivery with valid signature but unknown reference writes no settlement
under/over amount and wrong currency each produce a mismatch anomaly and NO settlement, even with a valid signature
same (provider, providerEventId) settled exactly once; a second delivery (and a replayed signed body) is a no-op; terminal-state guard refuses re-settlement
another buyer's order answers exactly like a nonexistent one (no existence oracle); verify gate enforces ownership before any provider round-trip
a signed webhook whose reference the (stub) provider says is not success settles NOTHING; a legitimate provider success settles

entries.area: Browser claim has no settlement power
entries.case: checkout client returns server snapshots only; the popup onSuccess path resolves to a server verify, and no client code path writes a payment status
webhook-then-verify and verify-then-webhook both settle exactly once; the in-flight claim serialises the two channels
attempt cap (5) enforced; a concurrent initiation joins the in-flight attempt instead of forking a second transaction

a PAYHERO payment row is visible but verifies as provider_retired with ZERO provider calls; backend registry answers 404 with 'retired' for PAYHERO and mounts no payhero webhook route; no PAYHERO_* config field remains
Prisma model default is PAYSTACK; the SQLAlchemy mirror matches (test_models compares the parsed schema); the manual migration is additive (SET DEFAULT only)
other-tenant Cloudinary, /raw/ and /video/ deliveries, external URLs, and cross-project Supabase all refused; own image/storage URLs accepted; fail-closed when env unconfigured
limiter wiring verified via the shared rate-limit module (fail-open without Redis, 429 shape covered where Redis is faked); the payment routes' limits were already pinned by the lifecycle suite

GAP: headers are emitted by the framework from next.config.ts and are exercised implicitly by the passing production build, but no automated assertion inspects the response headers in this environment. Recommended: a route test asserting Content-Security-Policy / Strict-Transport-Security on a 200 response (left as a noted gap, not claimed covered).
